chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Six or seven years in California with Eddie Heywood
summary: He went west with Eddie Heywood in the early 1940s, returned to New York for the Three Deuces and Cafe Society, then got very sick and only came East in 1948 to play with Edmond Hall.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Was it '47 he died, hah? Well that's right, in '47 -- oh in the '40s I was out -- I was out West. That's why I didn't run into anybody. I was out on the west coast with Eddie Hayward (PHONETIC).
And I think now that you mention it -- I think he may have been out of the band for a few months or something when he wasn't feeling well. And then he came back and then --
Yeah. But I was -- I was out on the west coast with Eddie Hayward (PHONETIC).
You were in California for a long time.

Well, quite a while. I would say about six or seven years. Off and on. I went out there with Eddie and I think it was the last of '40 -- around '43 or something like that -- or '44. And we -- and then we came back to New York and played the Three Deuces I think. We went back again and then came back again and played the Cafe Society Uptown. Then we went back again, and that's when I stayed out there and I got sick out there. Very sick.
And I didn't come East until '48. I think it was the fall of '48. I came to Boston to play with Edmond Hall.
